projectBackground.name: Fjord Crossing Viaduct — Approach Spans
projectBackground.timeline: Design check due in two weeks
projectBackground.context: The approach spans are being verified before tender. The checker has queried stress, expansion and scour.

manager.name: Ingrid Solberg
manager.note: A bridge has to be right the first time. Show the load path, the number and the margin.

assignment.title: Verify the approach span design
assignment.brief: Calculate moment, stress and thermal movement, check spans in Excel, answer the scour question and write the check note.

documents.name: Span Data
documents.note: Simply supported 12 m span; uniform load 20 kN/m; section modulus 4,500,000 mm³.

documents.name: Deck Data
documents.note: Continuous deck length 60 m; temperature range 40 K; steel expansion 12e-6 per K.

documents.name: Inspection Report
documents.note: Erosion around pier 2 foundation noted after floods.

tasks.title: Maximum Bending Moment
tasks.prompt: Simply supported span L = 12 m with uniform load w = 20 kN/m. M = wL²/8. What is M (kNm)?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Bending Stress
tasks.prompt: M = 360 kNm and section modulus Z = 4,500,000 mm³. What is stress M/Z (MPa)?
tasks.reasoning: Stress is moment over section modulus.
tasks.mistake: Mixing kNm with mm³ gives a result 1,000x off.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Thermal Movement
tasks.prompt: Deck 60 m long, ΔT 40 K, α = 12e-6 per K. ΔL = α x L x ΔT. What is ΔL (mm)?
tasks.reasoning: Movement must be accommodated by bearings and joints.
tasks.tip: Design joints for the full range.
tasks.mistake: Ignoring thermal movement cracks the deck or bearings.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Scour
tasks.prompt: Erosion is found around a pier foundation after floods. The main concern is:
options: Scour undermining the foundation and risking collapse
tasks.reasoning: Scour is a leading cause of bridge failures.
tasks.mistake: Treating erosion as cosmetic can lead to collapse.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Span Moment Table (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Maximum moment M = w x L^2 / 8 in column D for each span.
tasks.reasoning: S3 has the largest moment despite the lowest load: length is squared.
tasks.tip: Rank spans by moment to find the critical one.
tasks.mistake: Judging by load alone picks the wrong span.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Check Note
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence design check note for the checker.
tasks.modelAnswer: The 12 m span moment is 360 kNm and the stress is 80 MPa, which is within the allowable limit for the section. Thermal movement over the 60 m deck is 28.8 mm and the expansion joints are specified for at least 35 mm. The pier 2 erosion indicates scour risk; I recommend a scour assessment, riprap protection and inspection after every flood. All results are subject to independent checking.
tasks.reasoning: A good check note gives the numbers, the margin and the open risk.
tasks.mistake: A note with no open risks is not credible.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Flood That Moved the Pier
caseStudy.background: A river bridge failed after a flood because scour removed the soil beneath a pier. The post-flood inspection had been postponed.
caseStudy.challenges: Scour was not part of the inspection plan.
questions: What inspection trigger would you set?
caseStudy.solution: Vertex added flood-triggered inspections and riprap protection to its standards.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Water is the bridge's biggest enemy; inspect after floods.
